status: Read-only design study; no scene-reflection renderer implemented
observedProblem: Galileo panel geometry is clearer, but constant-colour panes with the existing sky/ground approximation do not reflect the visible campus. This remains conspicuous at walking height.
localEvidence: shaders/campus_ground.fsh computes an analytic environment from the reflected direction and mixes it with each pane's base colour.
client/CampusShadows.java already demonstrates an offscreen map-mesh pass with explicit GL state restoration and resource/world lifecycle handling.
The current renderer uses texture units 0 through 11; any additional texture unit must be checked against actual hardware limits.
The source wall polygons provide candidate facade planes; the test views at cameras 42 through 46 are retained for comparisons.

primaryReferences.facts: A cubemap has six square faces and is sampled by a direction vector. Seamless filtering across faces is a separate setting.
A texture image can be attached to an offscreen framebuffer; a cube face can be selected with glFramebufferTexture2D.

candidateApproaches.inference: A mirrored-camera render can give correct perspective for one selected facade plane. Select a nearby visible pane plane and apply its reflection only to coplanar glass; other elevations retain the existing fallback.
risksToVerify: Correct world/camera coordinates, winding and mirrored projection
Clip geometry behind the reflecting plane without opening visible holes
Restore framebuffer, viewport, texture and depth state
Refresh after mesh edits and resource/world reloads
Measure frame time and inspect moving-camera seams

candidateApproaches.inference: Broader directional coverage, but six captures add cost and a probe at one position gives inaccurate parallax on distant panes. This is a fallback research option, not a promise of accurate reflections everywhere.

nextExperiment: Prototype a bounded planar map-mesh reflection outside the production build inputs. Compare the same five native views, movement, day/night and actual TNT response before deciding whether to integrate it.
limits: Neither approach creates interiors. Vanilla blocks, players and mobs need explicit integration to appear; do not claim them as reflected until tested. No new imagery API or paid data source is required for reflecting already-rendered geometry.
